title: Universal scalar comparison equations
statement: Let $\Lambda,S$ be commutative condensed rings and $c:\Lambda\to S$ a morphism of ring objects [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. Use the specified exact restriction of scalars, universal right-derived comparisons and section arrows [def-sfb-closed-test-scalar-comparison-maps] and the specified models and comparison maps [def-sfb-closed-test-scalar-model-diagrams]. Then UniversalCoherence(c) holds: its five equations express normalization against the right-derived unit on every complex, compatibility with the derived adjunction unit and counit, compatibility with pullback composition, and compatibility with the unit-square-counit exchange for every commutative scheme square [def-sfb-closed-test-derived-exchange-maps]. No flatness or preservation of K-injectives by restriction is assumed; no direct-image comparison is inverted.

proof.text: Write $R_Y=\Lambda_Y$, $S_Y=\Lambda'_Y$, and $r_Y=\operatorname{Res}_Y$. The coefficient square for any $b:Y'\to Y$ commutes: $c_{Y'}\alpha_{b,R}=\alpha_{b,S}b^{-1}c_Y$, since $\alpha_b$ is the component at the coefficient ring of one natural pullback-composition isomorphism. Pass to reconstructed section-ring modules. The internal/section equivalences preserve underlying sections, and identify scalar restriction, the specified geometric adjunctions, their derived resolution transformations and pullback compositors. Thus the hypotheses of the ring-sheaf change-adjunction lemma hold for these $R,S,c$. All subsequent equations can be checked there and transported back with their specified normalizations.

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 0FPI (lemma-adjoints-push-pull-compatibility); internal/section scalar identification as in the cited nodes.

proof.text: Apply the exact-square right-derived-unit lemma with $F=b_{*,S}$, $G=b_{*,R}$, $U=r_{Y'}$, $V=r_Y$ and the ordinary sectionwise identity. It gives precisely $\delta_b:r_YRb_{*,S}\to Rb_{*,R}r_{Y'}$. Apply it also with $F=\Gamma_S(W,-)$, $G=\Gamma_R(W,-)$ and $V=\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Ab}}$, giving $\gamma_W$. If $\alpha^S,\alpha^R$ denote computation units, their defining equations are $\delta_{b,QP}\,r_Y\alpha^S_P=\alpha^R_{r_{Y'}P}$ and $\gamma_{W,QP}\alpha^S_{W,P}=\alpha^R_{W,r_YP}$, with the degreewise section identities understood. These equations characterize the comparisons uniquely. In particular, for an $S$-K-injective $J$ the comparison is computed by a further $R$-K-injective resolution of $rJ$ and its computation unit; $rJ$ is never declared K-injective. Exactness of restriction, not preservation of K-injectives, is the hypothesis used here.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); exact-square comparison with its universal computation-unit normalization.

proof.text:
Use the forward direct-image comparison $d$ of the ring-sheaf change-adjunction lemma. It is the derived comparison induced by the equal ordinary composites $r_Yb_{*,S}=b_{*,R}r_{Y'}$, so has the computation-unit normalization of step 2 and hence is $\delta_b$, by that uniqueness. Use only its forward morphism. Suppress the canonical identification $r_{Y'}b_S^*\cong b_R^*r_Y$ supplied by the same lemma. Apply its adjunct identity first to $t=\mathrm{id}_{b_S^*M}$ and then to $t=\varepsilon^S_{b,N}$. This gives respectively
$$\delta_{b,b_S^*M}\,r_Y(\eta^S_{b,M})=\eta^R_{b,r_YM},\qquad r_{Y'}(\varepsilon^S_{b,N})=\varepsilon^R_{b,r_{Y'}N}\,b_R^*(\delta_{b,N}).$$
These are the specified derived unit and counit equations. No inverse to a derived scalar comparison occurs.

source.place: Tags 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); forward comparison and its adjunct equation.

proof.text: The ordinary pullback comparisons and their scalar-restriction squares commute before deriving: both paths apply the same inverse image to the same underlying sheaf map and identify the coefficient action using $\alpha_{b,R},\alpha_{b,S}$. For two composable maps this is the same geometric inverse-image compositor, with the coefficient square of step 1. The section-module scalar comparison leaves the underlying restriction map unchanged. Termwise exact descent therefore gives these same squares in the derived categories; the internal/section normalization identifies their pullback compositors with the specified derived ones.

Let $L_b=b_R^*$, $G_b=Rb_{*,R}$, and use primes for $S$-coefficients. Suppress the exact pullback/scalar identifications of step 4. The actual exchange is $\operatorname{Ex}=G_{f_Z}(h^*\varepsilon_f\circ\theta)\circ\eta_{f_Z}$, where $\theta:f_Z^*s^*\cong h^*f^*$. Start with $\delta_{f_Z,h'^*N}\,r_Z\operatorname{Ex}'_N$. Naturality of $\delta_{f_Z}$ moves it past $r_{X_Z}(h'^*\varepsilon'_f\circ\theta')$. Substitute the counit equation of step 3 for $f$, the compositor square of step 4 for $\theta'$, and the unit equation of step 3 for $f_Z$. Naturality of $\eta_{f_Z}$ then yields
$$\delta_{f_Z,h'^*N}\,r_Z\operatorname{Ex}'_N=\operatorname{Ex}_{r_XN}\,s_R^*(\delta_{f,N}).$$
Both sides go from $s_R^*r_URf_{*,S}N$ to $R(f_Z)_{*,R}h_R^*r_XN$. This is a substitution in the displayed unit--square--counit formula, and does not cancel either $\delta$.
